study: Herman et al. 2022, CHAMPS classroom-management TPD (middle school)
eval_evidence: IES-funded efficacy trial conducted by the Missouri Prevention Science Institute (Herman, Reinke, Bradshaw), a research team separate from the program's developer (Randy Sprick / Safe & Civil Schools); trainers and coaches were 'supervised by the program developer' but the evaluation itself was run by the independent university research team.
developer_evidence: Training was 'facilitated by a certified CHAMPS trainer supervised by the program developer', and an on-site doctoral-level coach 'trained and supervised by the program developer' delivered coaching; the study research team did not personally deliver the PD, and the developer supervised rather than delivered it.
cascade_evidence: Developer (Sprick) supervised/trained a certified CHAMPS trainer and an on-site coach, who in turn trained and supported the teachers: developer -> certified trainer/coach -> teacher (>=1 hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Wait-list control within school: control teachers 'continued their business as usual teaching and professional development' and were offered CHAMPS later. True BAU, no active alternative.
coaching_evidence: An on-site coach worked with teachers in the classroom and met with them individually for up to 1 hr on a weekly basis (minimum dose four visits), reviewing workshop content and supporting goal-setting — recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: CHAMPS changes the teacher's classroom-management practice within regular instruction; no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose is added.
maturity_evidence: Delivered in four sequential annual cohorts, each receiving training and coaching within a single school year; academic outcomes measured at the end of that one implementation year (spring MAP / SAT-10). Single-year program for each teacher cohort.
